content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty trigger: service=control-plane-az3-health severity=critical
incident-bot: Symptoms: control-plane API 5xx spike, KV-cache evictions, autoscaler thrash. Region: eu-west, AZ: az3. Links: https://ops.redwood.internal/alerts/2855554321

maya: acked. i'm on it — picking up pager. :wave:
pagerduty: maya acknowledged incident (pager id: PD-98765)

daniel: ping — any customer-facing impact? do we have a quick blast radius? cc @paul

maya: short: hosted API 5xx ~0.28% across eu-west-az3 for reads->model routing. Some dedicated pools in az3 are failing model shard loads causing fallback to az2 which is increasing tail latency. Support ticket volume: 3 customers reporting increased error rates.

lee: logs show kvcache eviction rate jumped after a restart on a subset of serving nodes. possible memory leak + autoscaler churn. snippet from node logs:
```
2026-03-14T03:12:08Z control-plane node-az3-12 kvcache: eviction=312 /s free=220MB
2026-03-14T03:12:11Z model-loader: shard-load-failed id=mdl-llama-7b err=OOM
2026-03-14T03:12:12Z autoscaler: scale_down node=node-az3-12 reason=eviction_spike
```

maya: i'm starting runbook: control-plane-az-failover-v2. Step 1: pin routing away from az3 for new requests, keep existing KV caches warm where possible.

maya: running command to update routing policy (dry-run first):
```
# query current routing weights
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://routing.redwood/api/v1/weights?region=eu-west
```

lee: if we shift weights, ensure canary of 10% to az2 first. we'll watch per-route SLOs. also suggest disabling autoscaler scale down for az3 to let caches stabilize.

daniel: agree. @maya after canary if metrics look good, bump to 50% then 100% for new traffic, keep model fallbacks allowed.

maya: canary started — 10% new requests routed to az2. tagging metrics dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/2855554321

support-bot: Creating incident ticket INC-2026-2743 for customer-facing comms. Notifying CSMs.

pagerduty: escalation: if no ack from SRE lead in 10m escalate to pagerduty-oncall-2. (timer started)

paul: on call lead stepping in. investigating cluster-level OOM patterns across az3. are there any recent deploys? @maya

maya: no deploys in last 30m. we see a pattern of repeated restarts on 3 nodes which triggered autoscaler thrash.

lee: mitigation checklist executed: 1) disabled aggressive scale-down on az3; 2) pinned routing to az2 for canary; 3) started node drain on unhealthy nodes to allow controlled replacement.

maya: running controlled drain now:
```
kubectl cordon node-az3-12
kubectl drain node-az3-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

maya: after drain, we see reduced eviction rate and model loads succeed on replacements. error rate trending down to 0.05% within 8m of canary.

pagerduty: incident acknowledged and handled by maya, lee, daniel, paul. no further escalation.

maya: rebalancing: incrementing routing back to normal over next 20m. will keep autoscaler relaxed for 30m to avoid thrash.

support-bot: Noted impacted customers (3) and created follow-ups for support to send status updates. ETA for full stabilization: ~25m.

daniel: great work. please open a postmortem stub and tag SRE, eng-runtime, and product. assign owner for root-cause enrichment: maya.

maya: creating postmortem: https://pm.redwood/internal/2855554321-pm

incident-bot: Condition cleared: control-plane-az3-health returned to normal thresholds. Incident closed automatically at 2026-03-14T03:50:00Z.

paul: quick notes for postmortem — investigate kvcache eviction algorithm under low-memory scenarios, autoscaler hysteresis tuning, and add a guard to prevent concurrent restarts across >2 nodes in an AZ.

maya: will file follow-up tickets for quant change and add playbook step to disable autoscale temporarily on similar eviction spikes. cc @support-bot for customer communication plan.

lee: :thumbsup: thanks team, handing off to day shift for follow-up.
